quotes.text: The challenge is that Copilot doesn't break permission rules on paper. Instead, it operates within those permissions, but changes the way the information is consumed, effectively flattening separation lines that used to exist.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Precisely explains why Copilot creates new oversharing risk.

quotes.text: The bottom line is this copilot without oversight doesn't just open risk, it hides risk. When you can't measure or see what's happening, you can't mitigate it.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A sharp, memorable statement on AI visibility.

quotes.text: Don't try to label everything on day one. Start a pilot with the libraries holding your highest risk data Finance, HR legal, define what labels those need, test how they behave
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Actionable advice for a staged labeling rollout.

quotes.text: Logs are only valuable if they exist when someone needs to consult them, losing visibility because data aged out of retention undermines the whole effort.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Practical reminder to align audit retention with regulatory needs.

quotes.text: Start with sensitivity labels, add auditing for visibility, and finish with insider risk to catch anomalies. Skipping that order leaves you patching holes after adoption is already underway.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Summarizes the episode's three-step governance roadmap.

takeaways: Copilot works within existing permissions but blends content from across the tenant, so permissions and DLP alone do not prevent sensitive data from surfacing.
Microsoft Purview adds content-level control: sensitivity labels travel with the data, while auditing and eDiscovery reconstruct how content reached AI outputs.
Roll out governance in order: sensitivity labels first, then auditing with sufficient retention, then insider risk management for high-severity signals.
hook: Copilot can surface sensitive contracts or forecasts to anyone who technically has access. This episode is for Microsoft 365 security, compliance and IT leaders preparing a broad Copilot rollout. You will learn how Microsoft Purview labels, auditing and insider risk management give you oversight in the right order.
